docs-links.description: Check every relative link and anchor in the project's README.md files and doc/ trees; a broken one fails lint.

serve.description: Serve a Python application with hot-reload.

run.description: Run a Python workload once for the host and forward its exit code.

entrypoint.description: Entry point to run (defaults to src/main.py)

port.description: Port (set via the PORT environment variable)

force.description: Regenerate uv.lock even if it already exists

workspace-sync.description: Synchronize Python-owned workspace state (pyproject.toml project identities).

deps-upgrade.description: Upgrade dependencies of explicitly configured experimental Python projects.

workspace-install-exec.description: Sync the uv workspace members and run `uv lock`. Declares no outputs: everything it produces is either a shared workspace file (the root pyproject.toml it rewrites, uv.lock) — which the workspace-files effect states — or lives outside the workspace in the machine-global uv cache and the resolved virtualenv.

workspace-sync-exec.description: Align every selected Python project's pyproject.toml [project] name with its resolved project name. Declares no outputs: it rewrites tracked source manifests, which the workspace-files effect states.

deps-upgrade-exec.description: Run `uv lock --upgrade` for explicitly configured Python workspace projects. It updates their resolved dependency set, not a Putnami Python framework release set. Declares no outputs: it rewrites the shared uv.lock and the root pyproject.toml, which is a workspace-files effect rather than a captured artifact.

lint-format-fix.description: ruff pass that APPLIES formatting (`ruff format`). The mutating half of the format check/fix split: it is one of the two lint tasks that declare mutatesSources, together with the project-scoped "sources" write resource the planner serializes conflicting jobs on. The lint pipeline schedules it only when params.fix is true; the read-only counterpart is lint-format-readonly. Every ruff task first syncs the uv workspace, which rewrites the root pyproject.toml — hence the workspace-files effect — and runs ruff through `uv run`, which resolves and downloads the tool (network) into the machine-global uv cache and writes ruff's own cache directory (toolchain-cache).

lint-format-readonly.description: ruff pass that only REPORTS formatting drift (`ruff format --check`, no rewrite). The pure-check half of the format check/fix split: it reads sources, never writes them, and therefore declares neither mutatesSources nor the "sources" write resource. The lint pipeline schedules it only when params.fix is false; the runtime picks --check from the same fix param the pipeline guard reads, so the two can never disagree.

lint-check-fix.description: ruff pass that APPLIES lint fixes (`ruff check --fix`). The mutating half of the check/fix split: it declares mutatesSources together with the project-scoped "sources" write resource the planner serializes conflicting jobs on, and the lint pipeline schedules it only when params.fix is true. The read-only counterpart is lint-check-readonly.

lint-docs.description: Documentation link check: every relative link and anchor in the project's README.md files and doc/ trees must resolve, with the exact case of the file's name. The task body is the SDK's docslinks.Job, shared with every language extension. A link may name any file of the workspace, so the check reads the workspace's Git candidate cut (the tracked files and the untracked files no ignore rule excludes) and its key is the workspace input `git:**`, which holds that cut: deleting or renaming a link target, or editing a heading an anchor names, moves the key, and an ignored file is neither read nor keyed. The project input names the README.md the check starts from, so the key does not fold the project's ignored build output. Outside a Git work tree the check reads the disk and the task has no key. It needs neither uv nor ruff.

lint-check-readonly.description: ruff pass that only REPORTS lint findings (`ruff check`, no --fix). The pure-check half of the check/fix split: it reads sources, never writes them, and declares neither mutatesSources nor the "sources" write resource. The lint pipeline schedules it only when params.fix is false.

test-run.description: Run the project's pytest suite. Ownership decision: pytest is still invoked with no coverage or JUnit reporter — no --cov, no --junitxml — so the run owns no coverage profile and no JUnit report, and its result travels as the structured testSummary payload parsed from pytest's stdout, plus the per-case testCases that the injected putnami_testcases plugin records in a scratch file outside the project. The ONE declared output is the reserved spec-verification report (featureVerification), written by the adapter's merge of the fragments the injected putnami_spectest plugin records for tests bound with the putnami_proves marker; it is optionalEmpty because a project with no bound test writes none. The artifacts the run otherwise leaves (pytest's cache directory under .putnami/bin/extensions/putnami-python, the uv cache and virtualenv, the __pycache__ bytecode trees) are tool caches that are neither captured nor restored, which is what the toolchain-cache effect states. TestPytestOwnsNoReportsUntilItWritesThem pins the remaining gap: the day this task grows coverage or JUnit reporting, the declaration has to grow the matching command-output files the Go and TypeScript test tasks already declare.

featureVerification.description: The reserved run-scoped feature verification report: the merged observations of every test bound to a declared check through the putnami_proves pytest marker. Absent when no test in the project bound one. Written per member under batching, so per-project attribution and cache restore hold for both the singleton and the batched run — a cache hit that lost this report would silently disarm the spec gate.

serve-run.description: Serve the project with hot-reload. Declares no outputs: it runs the entrypoint through `uv run` and restarts it on change. Unlike the Go extension's serve task (whose "process" effect is deferred behind a known cache-policy gap), this task already sets cache:false, so the external process effect it genuinely has is declared here rather than documented as a gap.

run-exec.description: Run the workload once through `uv run` and forward its exit code. Declares no outputs: it produces only the program's own exit status and streams. cache:false is what lets it declare the external process effect honestly.
